question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{4}\cdot {3}^{2x}-\frac{1}{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot {3}^{2x}-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot {3}^{2y}-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot {3}^{2y}-\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{4}\cdot {3}^{2y} & =x+\frac{1}{2} \\ {3}^{2y} & =4x+2 \\ {log}_{3}⁡({3}^{2y}) & ={log}_{3}⁡(4x+2) \\ 2y & ={log}_{3}⁡(4x+2) \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}{log}_{3}⁡(4x+2)\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{2}{log}_{3}⁡(4x+2).$
